key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-silicon trilayer combines improved charge transport with environmental protection, achieving 8.52% efficiency and retaining approximately 90% after 75 days.
engineering_relevance: The architecture offers a route to more efficient, ambient-stable hybrid silicon photovoltaics on untextured substrates.
method: Benchmark planar trilayer devices against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Use PEDOT:PSS for anti-reflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and enhanced conductivity.
Use graphene as a charge-transport interface and moisture-protective barrier.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 8.52% trilayer efficiency versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si, with approximately 90% versus 29% efficiency retention for trilayer and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si devices, respectively, after 75 days of ambient exposure.
watch_item: The reported 75-day ambient test does not establish long-term outdoor durability or scalable, defect-free graphene barrier performance.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
